credits.name: Site Management During Construction
credits.intent: Control soil erosion and sedimentation during and after construction (Case A) and provide basic facilities for the construction workforce (Case B).
approach: Case A: erosion control before, during and after construction follows [[ECSBC 2024 / NBC 2016 Part 10 Section 1 Chapter 11]]. Fertile topsoil of [[volume]] m3 is stockpiled at [[location]] and will be [[reused on site / donated to (name, location, quantity)]].

Sediment leaves the site only through [[desilting chambers / sediment traps / silt fences]]. After occupancy erosion is controlled by [[natural vegetation, storm-water channels with check dams, soil stabilisers]].

Case B: peak workforce is {{SSP2_Workers|#,##0}} workers. The project provides [[toilet seats and urinals, men and women]] against {{SSP2_SeatReq|0}} seats and urinals required (3 for the first 100 plus 1 for every further 100).

Housing is [[on site / outside the site with transport]]. The workforce has first aid, drinking water, PPE, dust suppression, illumination and an emergency alarm [[and a crèche where more than 50 women work full time]].
evidence: Narrative and conceptual drawings of the erosion and sedimentation measures [[drawing number]]; soil fertility test report [[if topsoil is not fertile]].
Calculation of workers against toilets and urinals, male and female (workbook tab SSP MR1-3).
Contract extract or owner declaration for the facilities; geotagged photographs [[dates]].
preempt: State where the topsoil is stored and what happens to it, and give the quantity for any donation.
Show the sanitary calculation separately for men and women.

credits.name: Differently Abled Friendly Design

approach: The project has {{Park_Total|#,##0}} parking spaces and provides {{SSP3_ParkProv|0}} accessible spaces against {{SSP3_ParkReq|0}} required. Each space is 3900 x 5400 mm within 30 m of [[main entrance / lobby]], with signage at least 2.1 m high and a painted symbol.
Entrances have a clear door width of [[width]] mm and a non-slip ramp of slope [[slope]] with handrails and tactile warning blocks at both ends.
Lifts have a [[opening]] mm opening and a [[car size]] mm car with audio and braille. Each of the {{Num_Bldg|0}} building(s) has [[number]] accessible toilet(s).
evidence: Dimensioned drawings of parking layout, ramps with slope section, toilet plan and section [[drawing numbers]].
Calculation of accessible parking and toilets (workbook tab SSP MR1-3).
Certification stage: geotagged photographs showing signage and accessible features.

Geotagged photographs of amenities and stops.

credits.name: Sustainable Landscape

credits.name: Heat Island Reduction, Roof and Non-roof
credits.intent: Reduce heat absorbed by paved surfaces and roofs.
approach: Exposed non-roof impervious area is {{NonRoof_Exposed|#,##0}} m2 after excluding service areas. Tree shade, open-grid pavers and hardscape with SRI 29-64 treat {{SSP4_NRTreated|#,##0}} m2, which is {{SSP4_NRPct|0.0%}}.

evidence: Site and roof plans marking each treatment [[drawing numbers]]; roof area calculation.
SRI test reports from a NABL laboratory or cut-sheets [[product names]]; tree list with canopy information.
Invoices and photographs at certification.

Roof areas under elevated solar PV and PV in contact with the roof can count as mitigation.

credits.name: Outdoor Light Pollution Reduction
credits.intent: Keep outdoor lighting from spilling into the sky and neighbouring properties.
approach: All exterior luminaires, including facade lighting, are fully shielded with zero upward light. The upward light ratio is [[value]] (limit 0.5%) and the CCT is [[value]] K (limit 3000 K).
Fixtures are [[fixed / adjustable within plus or minus 10 degrees]]; facade luminaires have defined optics.
evidence: Photometric data sheets showing ULR, CCT and adjustability [[product names]].
Exterior lighting layout [[drawing number]]; owner declaration.
Invoices and photographs at certification.

credits.name: Sustainability Initiatives
credits.intent: Embed sustainability in design, construction and post-occupancy use.
approach: Option 1: the integrated design team included [[roles]] from concept stage and held [[number]] meetings on [[dates]]. Workforce awareness sessions and vendor training were held on [[dates]].
Option 2: permanent educational signage is in [[common areas]]; a screen in [[location]] shows the building performance dashboard; green building guidelines are given to occupants.

Awareness-session narrative and declaration; photographs of signage; draft green building guidelines.

credits.intent: Capture at least the one-day rainfall run-off from roof and non-roof areas to recharge ground water and cut municipal demand.

The mandatory run-off volume is {{RWH_Req|#,##0}} m3, calculated from the surface schedule. The system provides {{RWH_Prov|#,##0}} m3 through [[tanks / pits / trenches / percolation]], with filtering media before [[tanks / drains]].

Percolation or hydrogeological report signed and stamped by a third party [[title]] where a percolation rate is used.
Geotagged photographs during and after construction.
preempt: Do not count desilting chambers or oil and grease pits as harvesting capacity.
Use the thin roof garden coefficient of 0.5 (below 100 mm) in V4.0, not 0.95.

credits.name: Water Efficient Plumbing Fixtures

Baseline use is {{WC2_Base_KLD|0.00}} kL/day and proposed use is {{WC2_Prop_KLD|0.00}} kL/day, a saving of {{WC2_SavBase|0.0%}}. Flow rates are at 4.1 bar [[or converted from 3 bar by Q2 = Q1 x sqrt(P2/P1)]].

Manufacturer cut-sheets or letters at the design pressure; for tenant-scope fixtures the lease clause specifying flow rates.

Treated wastewater and rainwater do not count towards the saving.

credits.name: Water Use Reduction for Construction

approach: Baseline potable water for mixing, plastering and curing is {{WC1C_Base|#,##0}} kL. Treated wastewater, admixtures and curing compounds reduce it by {{WC1C_Pct|0.0%}} against 10% required.
Treated water meets [[IS 456:2000 Table 1 / CPCB / SPCB]] limits as shown in [[test report]].

Brochures, test reports and invoices for admixtures and curing compounds with areas of use; owner declaration.

credits.intent: Segregate waste at source so it can be recycled or treated.

credits.name: Building Reuse and Sustainable Materials Procurement

approach: Option 2: the project procures {{PR_Civil|0}} certified civil products, {{PR_EM|0}} electrical / mechanical products and {{PR_Other|0}} other products: [[list products and certificate numbers]].
[[Major renovation: share of structure and interiors retained.]]

credits.name: Organic Waste Management, Post-occupancy

approach: The converter treats {{BMR_OrgPct|0%}} of organic waste and {{BMR_LandPct|0%}} of the {{BMR_Land|#,##0}} kg/day landscape waste.

credits.intent: Keep pollutants out of occupied spaces.
